chapter.title: Temporal S2 Cell Indices
chapter.para: The temporal S2 cell index type ts2index represents the movement of objects as a sequence of S2 cell identifiers. S2 Geometry is a discrete global grid system that decomposes the sphere into six level-0 cells corresponding to the faces of a projected cube and recursively subdivides every cell into four children at each finer level. S2 supports levels 0 through 30. Each cell has a 64-bit S2CellId that encodes its face, hierarchical position, and level. Increasing cell identifiers follow the S2 Hilbert space-filling curve and therefore provide a spatial ordering useful for indexing.

The ts2index type shares its on-disk representation with tbigint: both store a temporal 64-bit integer. The distinct SQL type exists to let the type-checker reject S2-specific functions when applied to arbitrary bigint trajectories and vice versa. The S2 cell identifier is treated as an unsigned 64-bit value by the S2 API, although its binary representation is stored using the existing 64-bit temporal integer representation.
Casts to and from tbigint are explicit (AS ASSIGNMENT) and binary-coercion only, zero-cost at runtime but requiring an explicit :: in SQL.

As with other temporal types, ts2index has four temporal subtypes: Instant, discrete sequence, continuous sequence with step interpolation, and SequenceSet. S2 cell identifiers are discrete spatial values; consequently linear interpolation between two cell identifiers has no spatial meaning and step interpolation is used.

sect1.title: Input and Output
sect1.para: A ts2index value is entered using the standard temporal syntax with the underlying 64-bit S2 cell identifier. The preferred textual representation is the canonical S2 token, which is a hexadecimal string with trailing zeroes omitted. The token length is at most 16 characters. An optional 0x prefix may be accepted for convenience. The value must denote a valid S2 cell identifier.

S2 tokens are preferable to decimal integers because they are the standard compact textual representation used by the S2 ecosystem. The special token X denotes the zero identifier in the underlying S2 implementation, but zero is not a valid S2 cell identifier and is therefore rejected by the temporal S2 cell parser.
The type accepts type modifiers (typmod) to constrain a column to a specific subtype: Instant, Sequence, or SequenceSet.

The functions asText, asBinary, and asHexWKB serialize a ts2index value, and ts2indexFromBinary and ts2indexFromHexWKB reconstruct it. The hexadecimal WKB form lets a temporal S2 index column round-trip through a text-based COPY.

sect1.para: A ts2index value shares the same on-disk representation as tbigint. The binary-coercion cast between them is explicit, requiring ::, so S2-specific functions cannot be silently called on arbitrary bigint trajectories.

sect1.para: These functions convert an ordinary geometry into an S2 cell or cell set covering it at a specified level. S2 operates on the sphere, and therefore the coverage is based on the geodetic interpretation of the input coordinates. A tgeompoint overload is accepted only when its SRID is 4326.

sect1.title: Hierarchy
sect1.para: S2 cells form a quadtree hierarchy. Every non-leaf cell has four children and every cell has a unique parent at each coarser level. Levels range from 0 to 30.

sect1.title: Hilbert Ordering
sect1.para: S2 cell identifiers are ordered according to the S2 Hilbert space-filling curve. Consequently, the numerical order of valid S2 cell identifiers provides a spatial ordering, although nearby cells are not guaranteed to be adjacent in every situation. This ordering is particularly useful for sorting, range construction, and index building.

sect1.title: Metrics
sect1.para: S2 cells are spherical cells. Metric functions therefore use spherical measurements. For areas, the supported units are km2, m2, and rads2. For lengths, the supported units are km, m, and rads.

sect1.title: Bounding-box operators
sect1.para: The bounding-box operators use the temporal S2 cell extent and its time period. The spatial extent is represented by the geodetic extent of the S2 cell boundaries.

sect1.title: Spatiotemporal Relationships
sect1.para: The spatiotemporal relationships evaluate a ts2index argument through its per-instant S2 cell-boundary geometry. Unlike a planar tile system, S2 cell boundaries are spherical geodesic edges. The implementation therefore uses the geodetic interpretation of the S2 cell footprint.

Each relationship has three quantified forms: the e-prefixed ever form returns true when the relationship holds at some instant, the a-prefixed always form when it holds at every instant, and the t-prefixed temporal form returns a tbool of the instant-by-instant result. Every form accepts the argument orderings (geometry,ts2index), (ts2index,geometry), and (ts2index,ts2index).

sect1.title: Indexing
sect1.para: GiST and SP-GiST operator classes are defined so that the bounding-box operators of the previous sections can be used with corresponding indexes.

The initial implementation uses the temporal S2 cell extent and time period as the indexed bounding box. A later optimization may exploit the fact that S2CellIds follow a Hilbert space-filling curve and that the descendants of an S2 cell form a contiguous identifier interval.
